title: Heave Plates
text:
← All research topics

  
     
    Heave Plates
  

      
        
          
           
          
        
      

  
    
      Paper
      
        Validated CFD framework
        Single heave plate forced oscillations
        
          Numerical analysis of forced heave oscillations for an FOWT column
          with a heave plate using overset mesh
        
        
          Ocean Engineering 341, 122736 (2025)
          OpenFOAMOverset meshSA-DDES
          DOI
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          Can a three-dimensional numerical method reproduce the nonlinear force and vortex dynamics of forced heave oscillations, while extending the analysis into motion regimes that are difficult to test experimentally?
        
        
          Approach
          Advanced overset-interpolation strategies were assessed in OpenFOAM, followed by validation against several force and vorticity experiments and comparison of turbulence models.
        
        
          What the study shows
          
            Improved overset interpolation reduces artificial vortex errors.
            SA-DDES provides the strongest agreement among the tested turbulence models.
            The validated model reveals abnormal nonlinear added-mass behaviour at very low KC.
          
        
      

      
        
          
           
            Dimensionless vorticity contours between OpenFOAM and PIV experiments.
          
        
      
    
  

  
    
      Paper
      
        Combined experiments and simulations
        Double heave plates
        
          Hydrodynamic characteristics of double heave plates: A combined
          experimental and numerical investigation
        
        
          Research manuscript
          Forced oscillationPIVOpenFOAMSTAR-CCM+
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          When does a second plate improve added mass and damping, and when do inter-plate flow confinement and phase lag undermine the expected benefit?
        
        
          Approach
          Forced-oscillation and PIV measurements were combined with two numerical solvers while varying plate diameter, spacing ratio, KC, and non-dimensional frequency.
        
        
          What the study shows
          
            A second plate does not automatically increase added mass or damping.
            At high frequency, phase lag of the entrapped water produces a marked added-mass drop.
            Small spacing restricts vortex shedding; a practical spacing of L/Dp > 0.25 is recommended.
            A larger upper plate offers the strongest overall engineering balance among the tested arrangements.
          
        
      

      
        
          
           
            Spacing influence on the double heave plate damping performance.
          
        
      
    
  

  
    
      Paper
      
        Coupled FSI
        Reinforcement design for single heave plates
        
          Coupled hydro-structural analysis of reinforced heave plates under
          forced oscillations
        
        
          Research manuscript
          STAR-CCM+ULS / SLSFatigue
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          How can a thin heave plate remain structurally safe at full scale without sacrificing the vortex-driven damping that makes the device effective?
        
        
          Approach
          A validated two-way FSI framework evaluates six reinforcement strategies under an extreme forced-heave case, considering hydrodynamics, ULS, SLS, deformation, and fatigue life together.
        
        
          Preferred design · R3 full radial bracing
          
            −70.1%maximum stress
            −97.7%deformation
            +1.8%structural mass
            −13%hydrodynamic damping
          
          R3 remains below the fatigue limit and provides the best stiffness-to-mass balance among the evaluated configurations.
        
      

      
        
          
           
            Stress distributions at the instant of maximum stress for the six reinforced plate designs.

title: Wenzhe Zhang
text:
About Me
  
    I am a Ph.D. Candidate in Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering at
    Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM), Spain.
  
  
    I was born in 1999 in a small town in Anhui Province, China. I received my
    bachelor’s and master’s degrees from Wuhan University of Technology (WHUT)
    in 2020 and 2023, respectively. Since September 2023, I have been pursuing
    a PhD at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM), supported by an FPI
    fellowship from the Spanish Government.
  
  
    Before beginning my PhD, my research focused on ship–bridge collisions,
    risk and reliability analysis, and protective fender design. I continue to
    collaborate with colleagues in these areas, particularly on transferring
    collision-safety knowledge to offshore structures. I graduated with
    distinction from WHUT at both the undergraduate and master’s levels. During
    my studies, I received several scholarships and honours for academic
    achievement, student leadership, and community engagement. My master’s
    thesis was also recognised as an Outstanding Thesis in Hydraulic
    Engineering among China’s higher education institutions.
  
  
    My doctoral research focuses on the hydrodynamics of heave plates for
    floating offshore platforms. I combine physical experiments with
    high-fidelity CFD simulations, using experimental measurements to calibrate
    and validate numerical models. Through this work, I developed an
    OpenFOAM-based forced-oscillation testing framework that achieved accuracy
    among the highest reported to date. I have investigated the hydrodynamic
    performance of single, double, and perforated heave plates, providing
    practical guidance for engineering applications. Building on my background
    in structural mechanics, I have also conducted full-scale fluid–structure
    interaction analyses to examine failure modes and optimise stiffener
    configurations.
  
  
    As my doctoral research enters its final stage, my interests are expanding
    towards floating platforms for offshore renewable energy. Current topics
    include floating photovoltaic systems, the co-location of different
    renewable-energy technologies, shared mooring systems, and offshore
    structural safety. I welcome opportunities to exchange ideas and develop
    collaborations in these areas.
    I am also interested in suitable postdoctoral opportunities and
    expect to defend my PhD thesis around July 2027.
  
  
    Outside academia, I am an amateur photographer with a passion for natural
    landscapes. Badminton is my favourite sport, and I also enjoy watching
    football, especially when Spain is playing. ¡Vamos, España!

title: Collisions
text:
← All research topics

  
     
    Collisions
    
      Collision mechanics, rapid safety assessment, time-dependent reliability,
      and protective systems for bridges, ships, and offshore wind turbines.
    
  

  
    
      Paper
      
        Systematic technology review
        Protective technologies for bridges
        
          Review on the protective technologies of bridge against vessel collision
        
        
          Thin-Walled Structures 201, 112013 (2024)
          Active avoidancePassive protectionTechnology comparison
          DOI
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          How should available vessel-collision protection technologies be classified, compared, and selected for different bridge and navigation scenarios?
        
        
          Approach
          The review connects recent collision accidents with two protection pathways: active collision avoidance and passive anti-collision structures. Active systems are organised by input, analysis, and action, while passive structures are classified into six design families.
        
        
          What the study contributes
          
            A unified map from accident causes to active and passive protection measures.
            A comparison of operating principles, advantages, limitations, and suitable application conditions.
            Transferable concepts from adjacent fields, including vessel-vessel avoidance and metamaterial structures.
          
        
      

      
        
          
           
            Systematic technical review for protections.
          
        
      
    
  

  
    
      Paper
      
        Physics-informed machine learning
        Rapid ship-bridge collision safety assessment
        
          Physics-informed multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model with data
          augmentation for ship-bridge collision safety assessment
        
        
          Ocean Engineering 362, 126339 (2026)
          MLPData augmentationSHAP
          DOI
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          Can physical prior knowledge overcome a small real-world dataset and support rapid, interpretable screening of bridge anti-collision performance?
        
        
          Approach
          A dataset of 50 bridge assessment cases and nine ship, channel, and bridge features is expanded through two physics-informed strategies. MLP predictions are evaluated by repeated five-fold cross-validation, compared with SVM and random forest models, and interpreted using SHAP.
        
        
          What the study shows
          
            Both augmentation strategies improve the baseline model, with different precision-recall trade-offs.
            The transformation-augmented MLP achieves 80% prediction accuracy.
            Ship tonnage and navigable clearance width are the two most influential features.
          
        
      

      
        
          
           
            MLP data-driven model for fast ship-bridge collision safety assessment.
          
        
      

    
  

  
    
      Paper
      
        Time-dependent reliability
        Aged reinforced-concrete bridges under ship impact
        
          Reliability assessment of aged reinforced concrete bridge under
          ship impact considering multi-hazards
        
        
          Ocean Engineering 326, 120772 (2025)
          OpenSeesMonte CarloScour and corrosion
          DOI
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          How do scour, reinforcement corrosion, and uncertain vessel impacts change the collision reliability of a reinforced-concrete bridge throughout its service life?
        
        
          Approach
          An OpenSees finite-element model is coupled with vessel mass, velocity, and impact-angle distributions and Monte Carlo simulation. Time-dependent scour and material degradation are introduced to compare newly built and aged bridge states.
        
        
          Time-dependent failure probability
          
            9.86%at completion
            30.20%after 20 years
            50.95%after 100 years
          
          Scour dominates the first two decades, while corrosion becomes increasingly important later; inspection around year 20 is therefore a key intervention point.
        
      

      
        
          
           
            Reliability for aged bridges under ship collision.
          
        
      

    
  

  
    
      Paper
      
        Crashworthy protective systems
        Metamaterial fenders for monopile OWTs
        
          Crashworthiness study of a monopile OWT with metamaterial-based
          fenders under vessel collisions
        
        
          Engineering Structures 345, 121559 (2025)
          Nonlinear FEA22 MW OWTMetamaterial fender
          DOI
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          Can an annular metamaterial fender protect both a large monopile wind turbine and the striking vessel while maintaining acceptable nacelle acceleration?
        
        
          Approach
          Nonlinear finite-element simulations examine a 22 MW monopile OWT struck by a 5000 DWT vessel at 2-6 m/s. Baseline and dual aluminium-foam-ring fenders are assessed under multiple impact velocities, operational wind loads, and wind-impact angles.
        
        
          What the study shows
          
            The enhanced fender reduces OWT damage to negligible levels while keeping nacelle acceleration within the 6 m/s² safety threshold.
            Vessel bow crushing depth is reduced by 14.53%.
            Wind direction changes both peak acceleration and structural damage and must be included in collision-risk assessment.
          
        
      

      
        
          
           
            The metamaterial fender for OWT.
          
        
      

    
  

  
    
      Paper
      
        Experimental, numerical, and analytical mechanics
        Axial crushing force of bulbous bows
        
          Study on the assessment of axial crushing force of bulbous bow
          for bridge against ship collision
        
        
          Ocean Engineering 255, 111411 (2022)
          Axial crushing testsFinite elementsIUM
          DOI
        
      
    

    
      
        
          Research question
          Can bulbous-bow crushing force be estimated efficiently enough for bridge collision-risk analysis without constructing a detailed finite-element model for every passing vessel?
        
        
          Approach
          Two bow models with transverse plates and longitudinal stiffeners are tested under axial compression. Experiments and finite-element simulations validate an intersection unit method derived from rigid-plastic theory, with an equivalent-thickness correction for longitudinal stiffeners.
        
        
          What the study shows
          
            Internal structural arrangement and collapse mode strongly affect crushing force, even for bows with the same mass and external shape.
            The finite-element model reproduces reasonable collapse modes and mean crushing forces.
            IUM is suitable for transverse-plate bows, while longitudinally stiffened bows require the equivalent-thickness modification.
          
        
      

      
        
          
           
            The quasi-static test for bulbous bow.
